issues.description: Method SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice: The problem statement explicitly requires calculateTotalPrice to be static and to operate on the shared static stock (problem_statement.md lines 77-81). The solution implementation declares calculateTotalPrice as an instance method (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java, signature at line 57) returning int and not marked static. The template's example Main uses an instance call shop.calculateTotalPrice(meal) (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 13-14). This mismatch (problem expects a static method, solution implements an instance method, and the template example uses an instance call) creates ambiguity for students about whether calculateTotalPrice must be static and how it should be invoked, potentially causing incorrect implementations or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent design and apply it across all artifacts. Preferred fix to match the problem statement: change the solution and template to use a static method signature — declare calculateTotalPrice as public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) in SealSaloon, update its implementation to reference the static stock field, and update example calls in Main to use SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(meal). Alternatively (if you prefer instance method semantics), remove the wording that requires calculateTotalPrice to be static from the problem statement and ensure the statement, template examples, and solution consistently document and use the instance method.
